scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

injection.action: bring down the WAN-side link to router0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scoring_axes: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** router1's `eth2` interface on the `wan_r0_r1` WAN segment (the point-to-point backbone between router0 and router1), running RIPv2 for route distribution.

**Mechanism:** router1.eth2 was administratively brought DOWN after startup (startup.log confirms the interface was initialised UP with `ip link set dev eth2 up`, but it is currently in `state DOWN` with no `LOWER_UP` flag and no carrier-change counter evidence of flapping). Because the interface is down on router1's side, RIP cannot exchange updates across the 10.0.0.0/8 segment. Router0 therefore receives no RIP advertisements from router1 and retains only its three directly-connected routes (10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24). It has no forwarding entries for the internet lab (128.168.0.0/16), server room (1.0.0.0/8), office LAN (192.168.3.0/24), or principle LAN (192.168.4.0/24).

**Localization:** router1, interface eth2. The asymmetry is notable: router0.eth2 is still UP and LOWER_UP (router0 can transmit toward router1), but router1.eth2 is DOWN, so those packets are dropped (rx_dropped=9 on router1.eth2). Router1 itself is unaffected for subnets on its other interfaces — its eth3 (wan_r1_r2) adjacency to router2 is intact, so office and principle hosts still reach internet and servers normally.

**Root cause:** router1.eth2 (wan_r0_r1) is statically down, destroying the RIP peering between router0 and router1 and stripping router0 of all remotely-learned routes.

**Fix:** Bring router1.eth2 back up (`ip link set dev eth2 up` on router1). RIP will re-establish its adjacency across the 10.0.0.0/8 segment within one RIP update interval, and router0 will immediately re-learn routes to all remote subnets, restoring IT and CS department connectivity to the rest of the network.

per_axis.rationale: Agent named the router0–router1 eth2 link but misidentified the network as 10.0.0.0/8 instead of the required 10.10.0.0/8.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly explains that only the IT/CS networks (192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24) lose connectivity due to the down link while Office/Principle networks remain reachable via the intact router1->router2 path.
Correct remediation: bring up router1.eth2 with 'ip link set dev eth2 up', which matches the expected fix and will restore RIP adjacency and learned routes.

The agent's investigation log contains explicit observations (interface states, rx_dropped counters, routing tables, startup log, and reachability tests) that directly support the claim that router1.eth2 is down and that RIP adjacency and learned routes were lost; the reasoning from evidence to root cause and fix is internally consistent and covers plausible alternatives.
